property_summary: For any inputs to initialize(...), the correct contract sets its baseToken state to the _baseToken argument passed (i.e. c.baseToken() == _baseToken after successful initialization); the mutant always sets baseToken to address(0) so for some fuzzed _baseToken != address(0) the mutant violates this.

For any caller and any _baseToken argument, after initialize(...) completes the contract's baseToken equals the provided _baseToken (reference); the mutant that assigns baseToken = msg.sender instead will cause baseToken != _baseToken for some inputs (when caller != _baseToken).

For every call to initialize(_baseToken,_nft,...), the reference contract stores baseToken equal to the _baseToken argument (i.e. c.baseToken() == _baseToken); the mutant mistakenly sets baseToken = _nft so there exist inputs where c.baseToken() != _baseToken and the property is violated.

For any inputs to initialize, the contract's public nft() getter returns the same address that was passed in as the _nft parameter; the mutant breaks this by setting nft to address(0) instead of _nft for some inputs.

For any inputs to initialize, after it returns the contract's public nft() equals the _nft argument passed in; the mutant assigns nft = _baseToken so for some inputs nft() != _nft and the property is violated.

For any inputs to initialize, the reference contract sets c.nft() equal to the supplied _nft argument; the mutant that omits assigning nft leaves c.nft() == address(0) for some (nonzero) _nft inputs, violating this property.

For any initialize(...) inputs, the deployed contract's public changeFee equals the _changeFee argument (i.e. changeFee == _changeFee); the mutant increments the stored changeFee by 1 so this equality will fail for some fuzzed _changeFee values.

For any inputs to initialize, the stored changeFee equals the _changeFee parameter provided (reference preserves exact assignment); the mutant that stores _changeFee - 1 breaks this by producing a stored changeFee not equal to the input for some inputs.

For any inputs to initialize, the reference preserves the provided _changeFee into the public changeFee state variable (c.changeFee() == _changeFee), whereas the mutant sets changeFee to 0 causing c.changeFee() != _changeFee for some inputs (any _changeFee != 0).

For any inputs to initialize, the contract's stored changeFee equals the _changeFee argument (i.e., initialize stores changeFee == _changeFee); the mutant doubles the stored value, violating this rule for inputs where _changeFee != 0.

For any inputs to initialize where the provided _feeRate is ≤ 5000, the contract's public feeRate equals the provided _feeRate after initialize returns; the mutant that ignores the parameter and sets feeRate = 100 will violate this for any _feeRate != 100.

For any inputs admissible to initialize, the reference contract preserves the provided _feeRate (c.f. feeRate getter equals the _feeRate argument); the mutant overwrites feeRate to zero so this property is violated for some fuzzed _feeRate > 0.

For every call to initialize the reference contract reverts (does not allow initialization) when feeRate > 5000, i.e. initialize succeeds only when feeRate <= 5000; the mutant removes that check and therefore allows initialize to succeed for some feeRate > 5000.

For any valid initialize(...) call that does not revert, the reference contract sets initialized to true after the call; the mutant (which omits setting initialized=true) leaves initialized false, so for some inputs the post-call initialized differs.

For any inputs to initialize, the reference contract always has initialized == true after a successful call; the mutant that emits Initialize before setting initialized can leave initialized == false when reentrancy via the emitted event (to a contract) triggers a call back to check or rely on initialized, causing different observable state — the mutant can result in initialized == false after initialize returns for some adversarial callee behaviour.

For any inputs, a successful call to initialize on the correct contract always results in initialized() == true at the end of the call; the mutant that emits the Initialize event before setting initialized can be re-entered by a malicious listener during the event (via a callback) and thus can result in initialized() == false after initialize returns for some inputs.

For any inputs, a successful call to initialize(...) on the reference contract always leaves initialized() == true at the end of the call; the mutant that emits the Initialize event before setting initialized can be re-entered by a malicious contract during the event and cause initialized() to be false after the call.

After any call to initialize(...) that returns normally, the reference contract guarantees initialized() == true; the mutant can be re-entered during the Initialize event (by a malicious recipient of the event via a contract fallback when the event's indexed topics cause a log gas stipend behavior) and leave initialized() == false at the end of the call for some adversarial listener, so the property is violated by the mutant.
